los.text: Identify the components of the immune system and link them to function
los.html:
ComponentWhereFunction
Red bone marrow (primary)Flat bones, vertebrae, ends of long bonesMakes all blood cells; B cells mature here
Thymus (primary)Superior/anterior mediastinum, behind the manubriumT cells mature: positive then negative selection; shrinks after puberty
Lymph nodes (secondary)Along lymphatics: cervical, axillary, inguinal, mediastinal, para-aorticFilter lymph; cortex = B-cell follicles (germinal centres), paracortex = T cells, medulla = plasma cells
Spleen (secondary)Left hypochondrium, ribs 9–11White pulp (lymphocytes) mounts responses to blood-borne antigens; red pulp removes old red cells and encapsulated bacteria
MALT (secondary)Tonsils (Waldeyer's ring), Peyer's patches (ileum), appendix, bronchiSamples antigens at mucosal surfaces (M cells); IgA
Lymphatic vesselsThroughout, except CNS (glymphatics) and marrowReturn tissue fluid via the thoracic duct and right lymphatic duct to the venous angles
CellsInnate (neutrophils, macrophages, dendritic cells, NK cells, mast cells) and adaptive (T and B lymphocytes).
